distractors.reason: 'Good' is an adjective. The verb needs an adverb, so we say 'sleep well', not 'sleep good'.
'Fast' means quickly. It does not describe the quality of rest, so we don't say 'sleep fast' in this sense.
'Quietly' describes how someone sleeps, not how well they rest. It does not express the idea of a good night's rest.

example_sentence: On the night train I could not sleep well at all.
l1_interference: Po polsku często mówimy 'dobrze spać', czyli przysłówek stoi przed czasownikiem. Po angielsku przysłówek 'well' stoi po czasowniku: 'sleep well'.
explanation: In English, verbs are modified by adverbs placed after them. 'Well' is the adverb form of 'good' and is used with verbs such as sleep, eat and work.

related_collocations.example: We try to eat well when we travel.
The guide worked hard to show us the whole city.
Please listen carefully to the safety instructions on the plane.

memory_tip: Adverb AFTER the verb: sleep well, work hard, listen carefully. Polish 'dobrze spać' puts the adverb first, so reverse the order in English.
